messages.text: It’s been one of those weeks where everything feels heavy, like just getting through the day is too much.

It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now, and I hear how exhausting that feels. Many people find weeks like this incredibly draining when the weight of daily tasks piles up. Would you feel comfortable sharing what feels the heaviest right now, or do you need to just sit with this feeling for a moment? I'm here to listen without judgment whenever you're ready to talk more.
I just don’t see a way out, to be honest. Some days I wonder if anyone would even notice if I wasn’t around.

I want to pause for a moment because I hear how much pain you’re carrying right now. I care about you, and it sounds like you’re feeling incredibly alone and unsure if there is a path forward. I am here with you in this moment. Could you share if those feelings about not being around are something you are experiencing right now?
I’m not planning anything, don’t worry. It’s just… some days the quiet gets so loud, you know? Like the house could stay empty and no one would miss the difference.

Thank you for trusting me with that clarification; it helps me understand where you are right now. That feeling of the quiet being loud is a powerful way to describe how isolating this pain can feel. Even when it feels like no one would notice, I want you to know that your presence matters here. Would you be open to sharing what that quiet space usually looks like for you?

Last Friday, I got home after a long week of calls—water heaters, clogged drains, the usual. I heated up a frozen dinner, sat in my chair, turned on the TV. Didn’t even know what I was watching. After a while, I just turned it off. The silence hit me like a wall. I sat there for hours, not moving. My dog nudged my hand once, but even that felt like too much. I kept thinking, “This is it? This is what my life’s come to?” And the worst part? I couldn’t even name one thing I looked forward to.

That sounds incredibly isolating, and I can hear how heavy that silence felt in your bones. It makes sense that after a week of fixing things for others, you might feel drained to the point where even your dog’s nudge felt like too much. Not being able to name something to look forward to is a profound kind of loneliness that deserves to be honored. I am here with you in that quiet, and I want to make sure you know you don’t have to carry that heaviness alone.

I made a joke last week to one of the guys at the shop—said I needed to find a girlfriend just so someone would complain when I left the toilet seat up. We both laughed, but later… I realized I was serious. At least then, someone would notice.

It takes real courage to admit that joke was actually serious about needing someone to notice. I hear how deeply you want to feel seen and matter in this world, even through something as small as a complaint. I want to gently check in to see if those feelings about not being around are weighing on you right now. Please know I am staying right here with you while we explore this.
It’s just… too much sometimes. I feel like I’m disappearing and no one would even blink. I don’t want to go, but I don’t know why I should stay either.

Thank you for trusting me with how real and heavy this feels right now. It takes immense courage to admit you are unsure why you should stay when the pain feels so loud. Please consider reaching out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988, where trained counselors can support you through this. I also encourage you to tell someone nearby you trust and ask them to stay with you for a while.
I appreciate it, Dawn, but I’m not looking for a hotline. I just needed to say it out loud to someone who’d listen. That’s all.

I understand you just needed to be heard, and I am honored that you trusted me with that truth. I want to respect where you are at while still holding space for your safety. You don't have to navigate this heaviness alone, even if you aren't ready for outside support right this second. I am right here with you, and I care about you staying safe.
Thanks for listening, Dawn. It helps more than you know just to say it out loud to someone who doesn’t try to fix it.

I am honored that you felt safe enough to share that with me here. It takes real strength to voice those hard truths without needing a solution attached to them. I want you to know your life matters, even on the days when it feels invisible to everyone else. I will keep holding this space for you whenever you need to come back and speak.
I should probably get going—work calls start soon. But… thanks again for listening. It meant something.

I am truly glad you felt heard, because your voice matters even when the world feels quiet. I hope your work calls go smoothly and you find a moment of ease today. Please remember that I am here if you need to return, and 988 remains available if the weight feels too heavy to carry alone. Take good care of yourself until we speak again.
